executive_summary: michael-inbox.cjs's drainInbox() reads unread Michael-directed session_coordination rows but never writes back a lifecycle column -- the same rows resurface on every invocation forever. Its own would-be consumer, michael-quiet-tick.mjs's inbox-nudge counter, independently keys on a different column (acknowledged_at vs. read_at), so even after the write-back gap closes the two would still disagree. A third filed claim (no michael-advisory.cjs sender) is verified as deliberate, spec-documented design -- Michael is receive-only by §1.2 -- and is explicitly out of scope for this PRD.

functional_requirements.title: michael-inbox.cjs's drainInbox() stamps read_at on every surfaced recognized-kind row
functional_requirements.description: scripts/michael-inbox.cjs:48-93's drainInbox() SELECTs unread rows (read_at IS NULL) and prints them but contains no write-back. Add an UPDATE stamping read_at=now() on every row returned in `rows` (the recognized-kind set, not the `orphaned` set -- orphaned rows are surfaced-but-not-consumed by design and must stay visible/unread), mirroring scripts/solomon-advisory.cjs:532's exact pattern (`.update({ read_at: now }).in('id', ids).is('read_at', null)`). Do not stamp orphaned rows -- they are intentionally left for a human/future-kind-registration to resolve.
acceptance_criteria: drainInbox() stamps read_at on every row in the returned `rows` array (recognized-kind, matched rows) via a single batched UPDATE keyed by id, gated on read_at IS NULL (idempotent).

drainInbox() does NOT stamp read_at (or any other column) on rows in the returned `orphaned` array -- unrecognized/untyped rows must remain visible on the next drain, matching the file's own documented 'surface, never silently consume' contract for orphans.
A second call to drainInbox() immediately after a first, over the same fixture data, returns zero of the previously-drained `rows` (they no longer match `read_at IS NULL`).
The --json and --quiet output modes are unaffected in shape -- only the DB write-back is added, no output contract change.

functional_requirements.title: Unify michael-quiet-tick.mjs's inbox-nudge column onto read_at
functional_requirements.description: scripts/michael-quiet-tick.mjs:113-115's inbox-nudge counter queries acknowledged_at IS NULL -- a different column than FR-1's read_at. Michael has no two-stage ack model (unlike Solomon) and no background/cron split (unlike Adam's SD-LEO-INFRA-ADAM-INBOX-SURFACE-NOT-STAMP-001 precedent), so read_at is the single correct lifecycle column for both the drain and the nudge. Switch the query to `.is('read_at', null)`, keeping the existing target_session and payload->>kind filters unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: michael-quiet-tick.mjs's inbox-nudge query is keyed on `.is('read_at', null)` instead of `.is('acknowledged_at', null)`, targeting the same `payload->>kind` in(inboxKinds) and target_session filters unchanged.
A test runs the quiet-tick's inbox count before and after a drainInbox() call over the same fixture rows and asserts the count drops to 0 post-drain (proving the two readers now agree).

No change to michael-quiet-tick.mjs's other counters (classify, grade, brief, feeder, rulings) or to the QUIET_TICK_INBOX_DIRECTIVE line's rendering logic beyond the underlying count now reflecting reality.

functional_requirements.title: Correct the stale 'documented no-op' comment in michael-register.cjs
functional_requirements.description: scripts/michael-register.cjs:406-416's michaelReplyMirror() comment still says the drain 'is a documented no-op' (true when child G shipped only the function structure, false once FR-1 ships the write-back). Update the comment to describe the now-real drain behavior instead of leaving a misleading claim in the code future readers would trust.
acceptance_criteria: michaelReplyMirror()'s comment and/or returned string no longer states the drain is a 'documented no-op'.
A grep/diff check confirms the stale phrase is gone from michael-register.cjs.
The rest of michaelReplyMirror()'s output (the drain command hint, the 'Michael sends nothing' line) is unchanged -- only the now-inaccurate no-op claim is corrected.

technical_requirements.description: No schema changes. session_coordination.read_at already exists and is already used by the exact analogous pattern in solomon-advisory.cjs.
No new sender script (scripts/michael-advisory.cjs is explicitly out of scope per the LEAD premise correction -- Michael is receive-only by spec §1.2).
All three fixes are additive/behavioral-only inside existing functions -- no new production files beyond tests.

test_scenarios.scenario: drainInbox() runs against a fixture with 2 recognized-kind unread rows and 1 orphaned (unrecognized-kind) unread row
test_scenarios.expected: The 2 recognized rows are returned in `rows` and get read_at stamped; the 1 orphaned row is returned in `orphaned` and does NOT get read_at stamped.

test_scenarios.scenario: drainInbox() runs twice in a row against the same fixture data (no new rows inserted between calls)
test_scenarios.expected: First call returns and stamps the 2 recognized rows; second call returns zero rows in `rows` (they now fail the read_at IS NULL filter).

test_scenarios.scenario: runQuietTick()'s inbox count is checked before and after a drainInbox() call over the same fixture rows
test_scenarios.expected: Pre-drain: inbox count > 0. Post-drain: inbox count == 0 -- the nudge counter and the drain now agree because both key on read_at.

test_scenarios.scenario: A row directed at the 'broadcast-michael' sentinel (not a specific session id) with a recognized kind
test_scenarios.expected: drainInbox() still surfaces and stamps it (the existing `.in('target_session', [sessionId, 'broadcast-michael'])` filter is unchanged by this PRD).

risks.risk: Stamping read_at on the wrong row set (e.g. accidentally including orphaned rows) would silently hide unrecognized-kind directives from ever being seen by a human, defeating the file's own documented 'surface, never silently consume' contract for orphans.
risks.mitigation: FR-1's acceptance criteria explicitly requires a test proving orphaned rows are NEVER stamped, only rows in the recognized `rows` array.

risks.risk: Switching michael-quiet-tick.mjs's column without also fixing drainInbox() would leave the nudge permanently at 0 (since nothing writes read_at either) -- silently hiding the very directives the nudge exists to surface, which is worse than today's honest-but-wrong acknowledged_at-based non-convergence.
risks.mitigation: FR-1 and FR-2 ship together in this PRD (not split across separate SDs) specifically so the column-unification never lands ahead of the write-back that makes it meaningful.

consumers: scripts/michael-quiet-tick.mjs (reads the same session_coordination rows drainInbox() writes)
Michael's own seat loop (reads the QUIET_TICK_INBOX_DIRECTIVE guidance line and runs the drain interactively)
dependencies: session_coordination.read_at column (existing, already used by solomon-advisory.cjs)
data_contracts: session_coordination row shape unchanged -- read_at is an existing nullable timestamp column, no new fields added
runtime_config: No new env vars or config flags
observability_rollout: No feature flag needed -- both fixes ship together in one deploy; the quiet-tick's printed QUIET_TICK_INBOX_DIRECTIVE line becomes accurate immediately post-merge

components.name: scripts/michael-inbox.cjs
components.role: Drains Michael's inbox; gains the read_at write-back in FR-1

components.name: scripts/michael-quiet-tick.mjs
components.role: Computes the inbox-nudge count Michael's loop reads; column unified in FR-2

components.name: scripts/michael-register.cjs
components.role: Prints the inbox mirror on Michael startup; stale comment corrected in FR-3

implementation_approach.summary: FR-1 first (the write-back gap is the root cause), verified green in isolation, then FR-2 (the column unification, which only becomes meaningful once FR-1 exists), then FR-3 (the doc-comment fix). One combined PR expected given the small total diff (~20-30 LOC), per this session's small-PR guidance -- split into separate commits per FR for reviewability.

smoke_test_steps.instruction: Run node scripts/michael-inbox.cjs --json against a live/fixture unread row directed at the active Michael session.
smoke_test_steps.expected_outcome: Row is printed/counted, and a follow-up direct DB check shows read_at is now stamped on that row.
The previously-drained row no longer appears (rows: 0 for that row).

smoke_test_steps.instruction: Run node scripts/michael-quiet-tick.mjs --json before and after the drain in steps 1-2.
smoke_test_steps.expected_outcome: The `inbox` field drops from >0 to 0 after the drain.
